hook: Germany's greatest writer, author of Faust, who also studied plants, bones and colours.

pages.x: Johann Wolfgang Goethe was born in Frankfurt in 1749 to a wealthy family. His father made him study law in Leipzig and Strasbourg, but he spent his time writing poems, drawing and falling in love.

In 1774, at 24, he published a short novel about a young man who kills himself over a love he cannot have. It made him famous across Europe. Young men copied Werther's blue coat and yellow waistcoat, and Napoleon said he read it seven times.
In 1775 the young duke of Weimar invited him to his small court. Goethe stayed for the rest of his life, as a minister in charge of mines, roads and money, and later as director of the theatre.

In 1786, tired of his duties, he slipped away before dawn without telling anyone, and travelled to Italy under a false name. He stayed nearly two years, drawing ruins in Rome, and came back a different writer.
He found a small bone in the human jaw that was thought to exist only in animals, studied how all the parts of a plant grow from one leaf-like form, and wrote a book on colour.
pages.fx: His idea that living things vary on a shared plan was an early step toward the theory of evolution. His colour theory was wrong as physics, but inspired painters such as Turner.

pages.x: From 1794 until Schiller died in 1805, he and the poet Friedrich Schiller worked side by side in Weimar. Together they made the little town the capital of German literature.

He worked on Faust for about 60 years: the story of a scholar who sells his soul to the devil, Mephistopheles, in return for knowledge and pleasure. "Two souls, alas, dwell in my breast." He finished it months before he died.
He died in Weimar in 1832, aged 82. His last words are said to have been "More light!" In fact he seems to have asked for the window shutters to be opened, to let more light in.
Goethe is Germany's greatest writer, and the country's cultural institutes around the world are named after him.
pts: Wrote Faust and The Sorrows of Young Werther
Also a scientist of plants, bones and colour
